draft.title: Budgeting before you buy
card: A budget is a plan that compares the money coming in (income) with the money going out (spending).
Income can be pocket money, wages or gifts. Spending can be things you need, such as bus fares, and things you want, such as games.
If income is more than spending, the money left over can be saved. If spending is more than income, you cannot afford everything on the plan.
To buy something costly, divide its price by the amount you can save each week. This shows how many weeks you need to save before you buy it.
draft.remember: A budget shows what is left over to save, so you can plan before you buy.

a.q: Why does a budget help someone who wants to buy a costly item?
opts: It shows how much they can save each week for it
It lowers the price of the item they want to buy
It lets them spend more than their income allows
It works out the best shop to buy the item from
a.why: A budget compares income with spending, so it shows what is left over to save. It does not change prices, and spending more than income means the plan cannot work.
a.clue: Think about what is left after spending is taken from income.

b.q: Zara earns $20 a week from pocket money and spends $12 a week on snacks and bus fares. She wants a $64 skateboard. How long will she need to save?
opts: 8 weeks
3 weeks
5 weeks
32 weeks
b.why: Zara can save $20 - $12 = $8 each week. The skateboard costs $64, and $64 ÷ $8 = 8 weeks. Dividing by her income of $20 would give 3 weeks, but she spends part of that income.
b.clue: Find what is left over each week before dividing.

a.best: It shows how much they can save each week for it

problems.detail: Why (b) says dividing by her income of $20 'would give 3 weeks', but $64 ÷ $20 = 3.2, which would mean 4 weeks of saving. Better: 'would give about 3 weeks'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and keyed correctly: 'shows how much they can save each week' for (a) and '8 weeks' for (b). One small issue: why (b) says $64 ÷ $20 gives 3 weeks, when it is 3.2.
